purpose: Paired diagnostic of a confirmed message-extraction defect from v0.17, not a protocol comparison.
question: When the parser preserves square-bracketed natural-language outputs instead of stripping them, are Director messages delivered to the CRAFT Builder and does the two-turn task show progress?

prior_failure.observation: All three Directors generated bracketed prose; the upstream plain-text fallback removed those spans, producing three empty messages and zero Builder-visible messages. A Windows GBK console also rejected a Unicode arrow during oracle candidate reporting.

adapter_changes: In the Director parser fallback, extract and preserve bracket contents unless they contain the literal instruction-echo phrase 'Natural human speech only'; if no bracketed prose exists, preserve the unbracketed text as before.
Set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 for the child process.

model_and_runtime.runtime: llama.cpp b11202, 24 GPU layers, context 8192, endpoint 127.0.0.1:8000; CRAFT Director temperature 0.7/max_tokens 500 and Builder temperature 0.1/max_tokens 250

design.director_schedule: seeded sample without replacement: exactly one call for each of D1, D2, D3 per turn
design.paired_status: same task, source structure, and scheduling seed as the stopped v0.17 run; stochastic model draws are new and not an exact replay

primary: number of Director public messages successfully parsed and delivered to Builder per turn, out of three
upstream overall_progress after each turn and at the end of the two-turn cap

analysis: Report every completed turn, including zero-delivery or zero-progress outcomes. Keep generated, parsed, and Builder-delivered message counts distinct. If both turns deliver messages and progress is nonzero, preregister a broader structure feasibility study before further inference.
